We need propose a retrosynthesis route with 1 reaction (i.e., one disconnection) for target SMILES: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]

Let's decode: It's a bicyclic? There's a phenyl attached to an exocyclic alkene? The target appears to be a cyclopentanol with CF3? Actually C:15 with three Fs is CF3 attached to carbon 15 which is attached to carbon 13? Let's parse: [C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18] So a cyclopentane (positions 9-10-11-12-13) with OH on C13 and CF3 attached to C13? Actually C13 attached to OH and C15 (CF3). So it's a cyclopentanol with CF3 substituent.

Also there is an exocyclic alkene attached to C2 which also attached to phenyl ring. So overall it's a bicyclic? The retrosynthesis hint: carbonyl-ene reaction forward: alkene + carbonyl -> new C-C bond, forming hydroxyl and five-membered ring. So retrosynthetic direction: we need to break the C-O bond (hydroxyl) and break the C-C bond formed, generating a carbonyl (ketone) and an alkene (maybe internal). So the precursor would be a ketone and an alkene that undergo carbonyl-ene to give the product.

Thus we need to find a template that corresponds to carbonyl-ene reaction (forward). Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with functional_groups_broken: "ketones", "C-C double bonds"? Actually forward reaction: carbonyl-ene consumes a carbonyl (ketone) and an alkene, forms C-C bond and C-O bond (hydroxyl). So broken groups: "ketones", "C-C double bonds". Formed groups: "aliphatic hydroxyls", "five-membered rings". Also bond changes: C=O broken, C=C broken, C-C formed, C-O formed, ring formed.

Let's search.
